rationale:
Issue #500 ('Indentation weird on named argument function body') reports dartfmt emitting an offside body for the block-bodied named argument `getter:` in a call that also has an arrow-bodied named argument `setter:`. The production hunk in lib/src/argument_list_visitor.dart addresses exactly that shape: when the first function argument is a NamedExpression and any other named argument is a FunctionExpression with an ExpressionFunctionBody (arrow), functionsStart is cleared so block-bodied and arrow-bodied named function arguments are formatted uniformly. The trigger is the upstream regression fixture test/regression/0500/0500.unit, whose input is verbatim the code from the issue body and whose expected output indents the `getter:` block body under its signature instead of offside; it is driven by the pre-existing runner test/formatter_test.dart ('regression 0500.unit') and depends on no API introduced by the fix. The minimized production patch equals the single 34-line hunk in the one production file, with the CHANGELOG.md doc-only edit and the fixture excluded, so no refactor, formatting, feature, config, or test-only change is bundled. Machine-generated strict evidence passes in both the original and post-minimization runs: selectors present/unique (1), buggy differential reproduces test/formatter_test.dart::regression 0500.unit, fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs clean, deterministic across 3 repetitions with 32 matrix runs, and full-suite buggy failures limited to the declared trigger. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so dart-lang/dart_style#500 is not a duplicate, and it matches the single allowed verified issue key.

Issue #500 ("Indentation weird on named argument function body", opened 2016-03-17, closed by PR #595) reports dartfmt emitting a block-bodied named argument (`getter:`) whose body is indented left of its own signature line, while a sibling named argument (`setter:`) uses an arrow body. The minimized production patch in lib/src/argument_list_visitor.dart adds exactly one hunk that detects the same shape: when the first function argument is a NamedExpression and any other named argument holds a FunctionExpression with an ExpressionFunctionBody (arrow), it clears functionsStart so all arguments are laid out as ordinary expressions instead of receiving block-function special handling. That is the mixed block/arrow named-argument case described in the issue, so issue, fix, and defect align. The minimized patch and production-fix patch contain only that behavioral hunk; the CHANGELOG.md version-note edit and the fixture file present in patches/original-commit.patch are excluded, and there is no refactor, rename, formatting churn, or feature extension inside the hunk. The trigger is the unchanged upstream fixture test/regression/0500/0500.unit whose input is verbatim the malformed output pasted in the issue body and whose expected output re-indents the `getter:` block body under its signature; it is a data-driven fixture consumed by the pre-existing test/formatter_test.dart runner and invokes no API introduced by the fix, so it is semantically equivalent to the reported defect. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs reports all gates passed with the single unique selector test/formatter_test.dart::regression 0500.unit failing in isolation on the buggy revision (3a50bd05), passing on the fixed revision (16a7677e) across isolated, suite, and reversed runs, deterministic over 3 repetitions and 32 matrix runs, with the buggy full suite failing only on that reproduced trigger. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and dart-lang/dart_style#500 is the sole allowed verified issue key, so this root cause is not a registry duplicate.
